RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-AAA1CF805A-66883
Requested service: Cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-14
Treating surgeon: Duval, MD (orthopedic surgery)

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for single-level anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (CPT 22551), dated 2026-08-14. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice (due by 2027-02-10).

Ambetter from Magnolia Health's musculoskeletal surgery program, including cervical spine surgery, is administered by NIA/Evolent, and the applicable clinical criteria for this procedure appear in Evolent Clinical Guideline 1759 for Cervical Spine Surgery (Guideline Number: Evolent_CG_1759), within the Evolent Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines effective July 1, 2026 – July 1, 2027 (Last Revised Date: December 2025). I have quoted below the specific language from that guideline that I retrieved directly from the publicly posted document, and I have not restated or paraphrased it as plan language beyond what is quoted.

For single-level ACDF, the guideline states that the procedure is supported "When ALL of the following criteria are met":

- "Cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy from ruptured disc, spondylosis, spinal instability, or deformity"
- "Failure of conservative treatment* for a minimum of six (6) weeks within the last six (6) months"
- "Imaging studies confirm the presence of spinal cord or spinal nerve root compression (disc herniation or foraminal stenosis) at the level corresponding with the clinical findings."

The guideline further defines failure of conservative treatment as one of the following: "Lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment; OR Progression or worsening of symptoms during treatment; OR Documentation of a medical reason the member is unable to participate in treatment," and it notes that "MRI (preferred study for assessing cervical spine soft tissue)" is an acceptable imaging modality for this determination.

My clinical record documents that each of these elements is met:

1. Radiculopathy from a ruptured disc: My MRI of the cervical spine, performed 2026-06-07, shows a "C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression." This is a structural finding of a ruptured/herniated disc causing nerve root compression, consistent with the guideline's radiculopathy criterion.

2. Imaging correlating with clinical findings: My symptoms — radicular pain and numbness radiating into the right thumb and index finger, with weakness — correspond to a C6 nerve root distribution, which directly matches the level of compression identified on the MRI (C5-C6 disc herniation, C6 nerve root compression). My exam also showed "positive provocative testing on the affected side" and a "neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level." This is the specific correlation between imaging and clinical findings that the guideline's imaging criterion requires, and I believe it was not adequately considered in the initial review.

3. Failure of conservative treatment for at least six weeks within the last six months: I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training (16 visits, 2026-04-10 through 2026-06-19), as documented in my physical therapy discharge note — well in excess of the guideline's six-week minimum, and within the six months preceding this request. In addition, I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-23 that produced only 4 weeks of partial relief before my symptoms returned. Taken together, this history reflects "lack of meaningful improvement after a full course of treatment," which the guideline identifies as one accepted basis for a finding of conservative treatment failure.

4. Duration and severity: My symptoms have been present and progressive for 12 months, unrelieved by rest, and now include documented motor weakness in addition to sensory changes and pain.

5. No contraindications: I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

Based on the MRI findings, the corresponding clinical and neurologic exam findings, and the documented failure of an adequate trial of conservative treatment (physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection), I respectfully request that Magnolia Health reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 22551.

I am enclosing/have asked Dr. Duval's office to submit the following supporting records with this appeal:
- MRI cervical spine report, 2026-06-07
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-10 to 2026-06-19, 16 visits)
- Clinic notes documenting NSAID trial (8 months) and corticosteroid injection (2026-04-23) and outcomes
- Physical exam notes documenting provocative testing and neurologic deficit
- Surgeon's letter of medical necessity from Dr. Duval

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of any additional documentation needed. If any portion of the criteria I have cited above does not reflect the exact version of the guideline applied to my case, I request that Magnolia Health identify the specific policy, version/date, and section actually used in the original determination, as I have not been provided that information beyond the general reason stated in the denial letter.

Please send all correspondence regarding this appeal to the address and phone number above.

Sincerely,

Rowan Jennings
